html:
The Gros Ventre, who call themselves A'aninin (White Clay People), are a Native American people of the northern Great Plains, in what is now Saskatchewan and Montana. Gros Ventre is French for "big belly", a name given by fur traders.

Their language is Algonquian and very close to that of the Arapaho, and they are thought to have split from the Arapaho before moving onto the northern Plains. Once horses reached the Plains in the 1700s they became mounted bison hunters. For long stretches they were allies of the Blackfoot and enemies of the Cree and Assiniboine.

Smallpox and war cut their numbers in the late 1700s and 1800s, and the slaughter of the bison ended their old way of life. Today they share the Fort Belknap Reservation in Montana with the Assiniboine.
